classification.difficultyReason: Use the given tangent gradient to locate the point of contact, then find both lines and their y-intercepts. The final part requires recognising the intercept segment as a vertical base and using the contact point’s horizontal distance from the y-axis as the height.

content.prompt: The diagram shows the parabola $y=x^2-3x$ and a tangent drawn at $P$. This tangent has gradient $1$ and it cuts the $y$-axis at $Q$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 25 graph below the stem and above part (a), printed page 209
spec.description: Blue upward-opening parabola and red ascending tangent, each with arrowheads at both ends. Black axes have positive-direction arrows and labels x and y. Black dots identify P on the right branch and Q on the negative y-axis. The origin label O sits below and to the left of the axes’ intersection.
spec.mathematics: Plot y=x^2-3x and y=x-4 at equal coordinate scales. The tangent meets the curve at P=(2,-2) and the y-axis at Q=(0,-4).
spec.answerVisibility: The student graph shows only symbolic labels x, y, O, P and Q, with unnumbered axes and no grid. Coordinates, the normal, R and the triangle area appear in answers only.

answer.worked: At $P$ the derivative equals the tangent gradient, $1$. $$\begin{align*}y'&=2x-3\\2x-3&=1\\2x&=4\\x&=2.\end{align*}$$ At $x=2$, $y=2^2-3(2)=-2$. Therefore $P(2,-2)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent at $P$.

answer.worked: The tangent passes through $(2,-2)$ and has gradient $1$. $$\begin{align*}y+2&=1(x-2)\\y&=x-4.\end{align*}$$
On the $y$-axis, $x=0$. The tangent then gives $y=0-4=-4$, so $Q(0,-4)$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A normal is drawn from $P$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $R$. Find the equation of the normal, and the coordinates of $R$.

answer.worked: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its gradient is $-1$. It passes through $(2,-2)$. $$\begin{align*}y+2&=-1(x-2)\\y&=-x.\end{align*}$$ On the $y$-axis, $x=0$, so $y=0$ and $R(0,0)$.

The base $RQ$ lies on the $y$-axis and has length $0-(-4)=4$ units. The perpendicular height is the horizontal distance from $P$ to the $y$-axis, which is $2$ units. $$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle RPQ&=\frac{1}{2}\times4\times2\\\text{Area of }\triangle RPQ&=4\quad\text{square units}.\end{align*}$$
